sentences.text: This petition is filed U/s 166 of the I.M.V. Act seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 13.10.2024 at about 00.15 a.m, the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-EV-0006, on Sarjapura - Bengaluru main road, Opp.
SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 D.Mart, the rider of the said motorcycle rode it in a rash & negligent manner, endangering to human life and lost control over the vehicle and suddenly applied the break.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down from the motorcycle and sustained multiple injuries all over the body and the deceased was died on his way to the hospital.

Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies and they have spent substantial amount towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement and contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EV-0006.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of sections 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petitions.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.10.2024 at about 1.15 a.m.,
(midnight), Opposite D-Mart, on Sarjapura - Bengaluru Main road, Sarjapura Town,
Bengaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EV-0006 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.3 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 20 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondents counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  SCCH-23  MVC.8514/2024  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2 : The evidence of PW.1 and police documents placed on record indicate that on 13.10.2024 an accident had taken place and on the same day a complaint was lodged against the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- EV-0006.
Based on the complaint, the jurisdiction police registered the FIR and took-up investigation, during which they got examined the aforementioned motorcycle from the IMV Inspector.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV report wherein it is opined by the IMV Inspector that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicle.
Therefore the rider of the motorcycle did not have sufficient reason to cause the accident.

The fact that yet he caused it leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving the motorcycle rashly &
negligently.

Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet (Ex.P.8) against him for the Kera Ram vs Koushik on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35811726/
3 offences punishable under section's 281, 106(1) of BNS.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 filed by the police is defective or collusive.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 cross examined PW.1 at length.
But nothing could be elicited from her mouth to disbelieve her evidence.
Moreover the respondents have not adduced contra evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners.
Therefore based on oral and documentary evidence, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE No.1 :
The petitioner No.3 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the sister, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and mother of the deceased.
The Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 10. ISSUE No.3: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS

: The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 13.06.2002, which indicates that he was aged (22 years 4 months 0 days) 22 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
11.
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the RTA.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was doing hardware business by profession and earning Rs.9,66,400/- p.a.
If the deceased was alive, he would have earned Rs.15,00,000/- p.a.

To prove the income of the deceased the petitioners have produced Income Tax Returns ASY 2024-2025, TDS Statement, Profit and loss account, Balance sheet of Navadurga Enterprises, Capital Account statement of Navadurga Enterprises, statement of account of deceased and Bank account of Navadurga Enterprises which are marked at Ex.P.14 SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 to 20.

On perusal of Ex.P.14 and 15 being the IT returns for the period 2024-2025 and TDS certificate which is submitted on 07.08.2024 i.e., before the death of deceased which shows he was income tax assessee.
Ex. P.16
Being the Profit and Loss account for the year ended 31.03.2024, which shows the total net profit was Rs.9,66,440/-

. With regard to authenticity of IT returns the learned counsel for petitioners have relied on the decision reported in 2018 ACJ 2745, in the case of Roopa N.C and others v/s Managing Director, BMTC and (2020) 5 SCC 327 in the case of Sangita Arya and others V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., and others wherein it is held herein as under :
"C. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss. 166 and 168- Compensation - Computation of income - Consideration of latter most income tax returns (ITR's)- High Court determined income by taking average of ITRs for 2002-03 at Rs.54,000/- p.a.,
2003-04 at Rs.52,405/- p.a., and 2004-05 at Rs.51,500/- p.a., held, erroneously disregarding ITR for 2006-07, showing Rs.98,500/- p.a., for filing almost one year after death of deceased, which is factually incorrect - Photocopy of original ITR for Kera Ram vs Koushik on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35811726/
4 2006-07 filed before Supreme Court, bearing rubber stamp of Department should not have been disregarded by High Court - ITR for 2005-06, SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 revealing income of deceased at Rs.98,100/- p.a., during previous assessment year - Based on evidence on record i.e., ITRs for 2005-06 and 2006-07,
reflecting income of approximately Rs.1,00,000/- p.a., to be taken as a basis for compensation - Impugned judgment set aside"
12.

sentences.text: In appeal there against, High Court rightly held that monthly income is to be computed on the basis of income tax return, where available -
To benefit of appellants, the High Court proceeded on basis of income tax return of AY 1997-1998 being the maximum in three years."
Wherein in these two decisions the pith and substance of these two decisions IT returns being a statutory document on which reliance may be placed to determine the annual income of the deceased.
In the instant case on hand, having regard to the contents of Ex.P.14 IT Returns the deceased income as per assessment year 2024-2025 is Rs.9,66,440/-.
Out of the said annual income, professional tax and income tax needs to be deducted.

5  SCCH-23  MVC.8514/2024 13.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 22 years.
His income is taken as Rs.77,570/- p.m.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 22 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged about 22 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.1,08,598/- p.m.
(Rs.77,570/- + 31,028/- i.e., 40%).
14.

Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 verma V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation, the 50%
of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

sentences.text:
On such deduction, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.54,299/- p.m.
(Rs.1,08,598/- X 50/100).
15.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.54,299/- p.m. and the multiplier "18" is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.1,17,28,584/- (Rs.54,299 X 12 X 18)

Considering the above facts,
I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,17,28,600/- under the head of loss of dependency.

16. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a daughter causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their daughter during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

17. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of Insurance Policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending motorcycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 21. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,18,44,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 40% Petitioner No.3 - 20%

Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 75% each shall be released to them SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 Kera Ram vs Koushik on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35811726/
7 through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,18,44,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 40% Petitioner No.2 - 40% Petitioner No.3 - 20%
Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 75% each shall be released to them SCCH-23 MVC.8514/2024 Kera Ram vs Koushik on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35811726/
7 through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

Draw an award accordingly.
rpc_texts: Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending motorcycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Accordingly issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
